why: Tier win rates of 44%, 50% and 59% can average the 50% a league must have, and team revenues of $8 to $39 million with profits under $2.5 million are believable for a professional rugby league.
Every country's format shares sum to 100%, and 83,000 to 1.31 million copies a year per country is believable for a children's publisher.
Every port's cargo shares sum to 100%, and 24 to 80 million tonnes per port (about 366 million in all) is believable for the main ports of a mid-sized country.
40 truffle shops taking about $0.86 to $1.08 million a month (roughly $22,000 to $27,000 per shop) is believable, as are the modest index movements.
Every region's milk-use shares sum to 100%, and 31 to 150 million litres per region is believable for a dairy co-operative.
A food-delivery platform with $460 million revenue, courier payments of 78% and overheads of 26% running a 4% loss is consistent and believable.
Convenience-store profits of about GBP 38,000 to 158,000 per store across estates of 95 to 160 stores are believable.
Each survey row is a subset no larger than the one above it for both apartments (4,860 to 1,244) and houses (2,915 to 376), so the funnel is consistent.
350,000 new shoppers with first-year contribution of $1 to $31 on 90-day spend of $44 to $263 implies thin but believable pet-supply margins.
Each route's two driver shares sum to 100% (negative where passengers per sailing fell), and yearly growth of 1.8% to 4.6% is believable for a ferry operator.
